Harvest Time: First harvest 40–55 days after sowing; subsequent cuts about every 14 days for up to six months (EcoCrop).
Yield / Year: 100000 kg/ha/crop (EcoCrop estimate: 10 kg/m²/crop).
Ideal Light Conditions: Prefers humid conditions and partial shade or cloudy weather. In full, exposed sunlight during dry spells, plants remain smaller and suffer from heat stress.
Ideal Soil Conditions: Moist, well-drained soil; tolerates some drought through water-storing leaves.
Layout: Plant beneath a medium-high canopy, Typical spacings range around 10–25 plants/m² depending on harvest style. Establish main plantings at the onset of the rainy season so roots and mycorrhizal networks are well-developed before drier months arrive.
Intercrop: Collard greens (couve-de-folha)
Companion Plants: Couve-de-folha (Brassica oleracea var. acephala)
Trees: Açaí, cacao, or legume shade/pruning trees

Harvest Time: 30 to 90 days
Yield / Year: 2 kg
Ideal Light Conditions: Thrives under partial shading (ranging from 30% to 70%). Full sun stresses the plant, forcing it to flower prematurely.
Ideal Soil Conditions: Moist, well-drained, fertile soil
Pathogens: Root-knot nematodes (Meloidogyne spp.), fungal leaf spots: Cercospora sp. and Alternaria sp.
Layout: Plant under mid-to-high canopy fruit/timber trees to filter direct sunlight and lower ambient temperatures.
Intercrop: Chives (Allium schoenoprasum) and true coriander (Coriandrum sativum).
Companion Plants: Cariru (Talinum triangulare), Ariá (Goeppertia allouia), Maniva/Mandioca (Manihot esculenta), Coentro (Coriandrum sativum), Jambu (Spilanthes oleracea).
Trees: Use mid-to-high canopy or fruit/timber trees: banana, papaya, citrus, or native leguminous trees.

Harvest Time: 50–60 days
Ideal Light Conditions: Thrives under partial shade or dappled canopy light (around 50% shade
Ideal Soil Conditions: moist soil, tolerates a wide pH range but demands high nitrogen
Pathogens: Leaf Spots (Fusarium & Cercospora spp.), White Rust (Albugo bliti), Collar, Stem & Root Rots (Rhizoctonia solani / Corticium solani and Pythium spp.)
Layout: Plant beneath medium-to-high canopy trees (açaí, cupuaçu, cacao, or banana). Documented bed option: 0.20 m between rows × 0.10 m between plants; maintain drainage.
Intercrop: N/A works as a ground cover
Companion Plants: Açaí, cupuaçu, cacao, or banana
Trees: ingá (Inga edulis) or gliricídia.

Harvest Time: 60 days
Ideal Light Conditions: Partial shade or dappled light rather than scorching, direct midday sun.
Ideal Soil Conditions: Well-drained, sandy-loam to medium-textured soil with a slightly acidic to near-neutral pH (roughly 5.6–6.5).
Pathogens: Foliar nematode (Aphelenchoides pseudobesseyi), Root-knot nematode (Meloidogyne javanica), Cucumber mosaic virus (CMV)
Layout: Plant jambu and other short-cycle greens in rows between trees like Gliricidia or Inga. Place them along bed edges or in strips next to taller crops like corn or cassava and young trees. Documented bed spacing: 0.25 × 0.25 m (Embrapa).
Intercrop: Arugula (Eruca sativa), Cassava (Manihot esculenta)
Companion Plants: Crotalaria (fast-growing green manure or nitrogen fixer)
Trees: Taller fruit or timber trees: açaí, cupuaçu, or cocoa

Harvest Time: Tubers approximately 8–14 months after planting (EcoCrop), as foliage dies back; short-day tuberization. Perennial: leave some rhizomes to regrow.
Yield / Year: 2000–15000 kg/ha/crop tubers (EcoCrop); up to 0.260 kg tubers/plant in the team-cited Trinidad trial at approximately 20800 plants/ha.
Ideal Light Conditions: Partial shade preferred (50% shade gave better tuber partitioning than full sun); tolerates full sun if moisture and nutrients are adequate
Ideal Soil Conditions: Moist, humus-rich, well-drained, fertile soil; pH as specified in the numeric EcoCrop fields (tolerates 5.5–7.5); ~22–31 °C; use the numeric EcoCrop fields for environmental screening.
Layout: Plant rhizome pieces ~0.6–0.7 m apart (trial densities 20,800–27,700 plants/ha). Use as a shaded understory strip under banana or between young tree rows. Pre-soaking rhizomes in 48 °C water for 10 min improves sprouting
Intercrop: Cassava, plantain, coffee (FAO Ecocrop intercropping list)
Companion Plants: Chicoria (Eryngium foetidum), Cariru, Taioba: shade-tolerant greens that share its moist, filtered-light niche (inferred)
Trees: Banana/plantain, Ingá (Inga edulis) or Gliricidia for light shade

Harvest Time: First fruit ~3–4.5 months after sowing/transplant (related P. peruviana starts ~130 days), then continuous picking for months. Pick when calyx turns yellow-brown, ~25–30 days after flowering
Yield / Year: No P. angulata-specific figure found; related P. peruviana 3000–12000 kg/ha (Embrapa)
Ideal Light Conditions: Full sun to light shade; fruited well in an agroforestry system (UNESP trial)
Ideal Soil Conditions: Medium-textured, fertile, well-drained soil with no previous solanaceous crop. Strongly responds to phosphorus: plants at 8 mg/kg P did not flower or fruit
Layout: Stake plants and thin to 2–4 stems. Spacing ~1–1.5 m between plants (typical for Physalis; verify locally). Place in sunny gaps or bed edges of the lower mid-layer. Species-specific field-trial alternative: 1.8 m between rows × 0.8 m between plants, with drip irrigation.
Intercrop: Not documented. (inferred) Short-cycle legumes or greens while young
Companion Plants: Gliricidia or Crotalaria nearby for nitrogen. Avoid planting next to other Solanaceae (Cubiu) to limit shared soil diseases
Trees: Light-canopy legume trees (Gliricidia, Ingá, pruned) or banana for partial shade

Harvest Time: Tubers mature in ~9–11 mo (280–330 days) from planting
Yield / Year: 15000–20000 kg/ha/crop tubers (EcoCrop); maturity 280–330 days.
Ideal Light Conditions: Sun to dappled partial shade (climbs trellises or living tree stakes)
Ideal Soil Conditions: Deep, loose, humus-rich, well-drained mounds; EcoCrop pH as specified in the numeric EcoCrop fields (tolerates 5.3–8.0). Avoid compacted wet soil; use the numeric EcoCrop fields for environmental screening.
Layout: 1.0 × 1.0 m on mounds with stakes or living tree trellises
Intercrop: Banana, cassava, maize, taioba, jambu
Companion Plants: Not independently documented.
Trees: Living support or stakes; specific support species not verified.

Harvest Time: Approx. 6–8 months from sowing to first harvest, then harvest continues for several months (general literature; verify locally). Seedlings transplanted at ~45 days
Yield / Year: Up to ~14 kg/plant/yr (≈100 t/ha) cited as potential; field yields are usually lower
Ideal Light Conditions: Full sun to light shade (50% shade used in the nursery)
Ideal Soil Conditions: Fertile, well-drained, organic-rich soil (trials added 2 kg compost per planting hole); slightly acidic, ~pH 5.5–6.5 (inferred)
Layout: Planted at 1.0 × 1.5 m in trials; 1 m between plants in other studies. Plant in sunny gaps in the lower mid-layer, with compost in each hole
Intercrop: Not documented. (inferred) Short-cycle greens while the plants are young
Companion Plants: Gliricidia (biomass suppresses Sclerotium), Crotalaria. Avoid other Solanaceae (Camapu, tomato) nearby
Trees: Gliricidia and Ingá lopped regularly for mulch; banana for light shade. Needs a sparse canopy

Harvest Time: Varzea cultivars ~8 months; terra firme typically 8–18 months (best interval 14–18 months in Acre); table cassava (macaxeira) 6–10 months. Roots can stay in the ground until needed
Yield / Year: Amazon average ~14 t/ha; 25–35 t/ha with improved cultivars (e.g. 33 t/ha for Aipim Manteiga in Amazonas); up to 45 t/ha with full technology (Embrapa)
Ideal Light Conditions: Full sun; shade slows root bulking
Ideal Soil Conditions: Well-drained, light to medium-textured soil; tolerates low fertility and acidity but not waterlogging. Responds to organic matter and P (Embrapa); use the numeric EcoCrop fields for environmental screening.
Layout: 1.0 × 1.0 m (Embrapa), or double rows 2.0 × 0.6 × 0.6 m (~11,800 plants/ha) with a legume in the wide alley. Plant stem cuttings 20 cm long
Intercrop: Cowpea (feijão-caupi), beans, maize in the wide alleys (Embrapa Amapá); Crotalaria, pigeon pea (guandu) and Flemingia as legume cover (Embrapa Amazônia Ocidental)
Companion Plants: Crotalaria, pigeon pea, Flemingia (green manures); Gliricidia in alleys competes less than Leucaena
Trees: Gliricidia or Ingá in widely spaced rows; also a good early-year crop between young Brazil nut, pupunha or Parica

Harvest Time: 60–75 days
Yield / Year: Leaves: 1.5–2.0 kg/cycle, Tubers/cormels: 1–2 kg/plant.
Ideal Light Conditions: Thrives in filtered shade.
Ideal Soil Conditions: Sensitive to prolonged drought, waterlogged soils. Maintain loose, high-organic soil; use the numeric EcoCrop fields for environmental screening.
Pathogens: Root and Corm Rot Complex (Pythium myriotylum, Fusarium spp., Rhizoctonia spp., and Athelia rolfsii), Leaf Spot (Paramyrothecium roridum), Root-Knot and Lesion Nematodes (Meloidogyne spp., Pratylenchus spp., and Rotylenchulus reniformis)
Layout: Plant on raised beds (leirões or camalhões). Mound organic soil 20–30 cm high to keep the root zone aerobic during torrential rains. Documented Embrapa planting option: 0.70 m between rows × 0.40 m between plants.
Intercrop: Cacao, açaí, banana, cassava
Companion Plants: Banana
Trees: Ingá (Inga edulis), Gliricidia, or Banana (Musa spp.)

Harvest Time: Bunch ~9–15 months after planting, then continuous harvest as ratoons (suckers) follow
Yield / Year: ~10000–25000 kg/ha/yr in agroforestry (higher in intensive systems)
Ideal Light Conditions: Full sun to light shade (about 50–70% light). Needs wind shelter
Ideal Soil Conditions: Deep, well-drained, humus-rich, pH as specified in the numeric EcoCrop fields, with evenly distributed rainfall; use the numeric EcoCrop fields for environmental screening.
Layout: Rows at 3 × 3 m, or 2 rows of banana between tree lines spaced 6–8 m apart
Intercrop: Cassava, beans, pineapple, taro, ginger, turmeric, coffee, cacao
Companion Plants: Inga, Gliricidia, Crotalaria, pigeon pea, Canavalia, sweet potato (ground cover)
Trees: Inga, Erythrina and Gliricidia (lopped for mulch), widely spaced guapuruvu or paricá, açaí, cupuaçu

Harvest Time: Perennial climber; leaves harvested as needed once established. Timing not documented in sources found. Propagated by stem cuttings
Yield / Year: Not documented
Ideal Light Conditions: (inferred) Propagated under shade cloth; partial shade (forest-edge liana), tolerates more sun once established
Ideal Soil Conditions: Sandy, sandy-clay or clay soil rich in organic matter; 20–30 °C (Embrapa Rondônia)
Layout: Semi-climbing shrub of 3 m or more, so it needs a trellis or support. Best cuttings are ~1 cm in diameter and carry about six shoots. Spacing not documented
Intercrop: Not documented
Companion Plants: (inferred) Not documented. Gliricidia or Ingá can act as living support
Trees: (inferred) Grows up a support tree or trellis: Gliricidia, Ingá, or a mid-layer fruit tree

Harvest Time: First pods ~2.5–3 years after planting, earlier for clones (general knowledge); 7–10 harvests per year in Rondônia agroforestry
Yield / Year: 600–700 kg dry beans/ha/yr with partial technology, >1,200 kg/ha/yr with full management (Rondônia SAF); up to ~2,100 kg/ha/yr in intensive 'candlestick' trials
Ideal Light Conditions: Shade-tolerant understory tree (grown under cabruca, rubber or Erythrina shade); needs temporary shade such as banana when young (general knowledge)
Ideal Soil Conditions: Deep, well-drained, humus-rich soil, pH as specified in the numeric EcoCrop fields (general); rainfall evenly distributed, no waterlogging
Layout: 3 × 3 m with banana between (Rondônia SAF); 4 × 4 m in Tomé-Açu systems (650 plants/ha); about 400 trees/ha in cabruca. Grown in rows beneath tall shade trees
Intercrop: Banana and short-cycle grains (rice, maize, beans) in year 1; açaí, cupuaçu, black pepper, Brazil nut in mature systems
Companion Plants: Ingá, Gliricidia, Erythrina as shade/nitrogen trees; banana (temporary shade)
Trees: Banana , Erythrina, Ingá, Gliricidia; permanent shade from rubber, Brazil nut, Parica or native cabruca trees

Harvest Time: Starts producing at a few years of age (about 3–4, general knowledge); harvest is concentrated in the rainy season
Yield / Year: approximately 15 fruits/plant/year for the best Tomé-Açu progeny; approximately 20 kg pulp/plant/year for one promising progeny. Processing yield: 1000 kg fruit gives approximately 370 kg pulp and 150 kg fresh seed.
Ideal Light Conditions: Needs shade when young (banana, pigeon pea, papaya); in production, shade above ~25% reduces fruit yield, so thin the canopy
Ideal Soil Conditions: Deep, well-drained, fertile terra firme soil; responds to liming per soil analysis; use the numeric EcoCrop fields for environmental screening.
Pathogens: Witches' broom (Moniliophthora perniciosa); use suitable resistant planting material and sanitary pruning.
Layout: 6 × 4 to 6 × 5 m; with banana and a timber tree, banana in the rows and timber at 20 × 10 m. Can sit between açaí or pupunha rows at 10 × 10 m
Intercrop: Passion fruit, banana, papaya as early shade crops; black pepper (2 × 2 m), Brazil nut, mahogany, açaí
Companion Plants: Banana, pigeon pea (temporary shade), Gliricidia and Ingá for mulch and nitrogen
Trees: Parica, Brazil nut, mahogany or açaí as upper layer (Embrapa multi-strata systems); Gliricidia/Ingá lopped for nitrogen

Harvest Time: Fruit from the 3rd year after planting; flowering Sept–Dec and harvest ~Jan–Apr in terra firme (one main season; in the floodplain fruiting follows the dry season). Planted fields in terra firme fruited throughout the year in one study
Yield / Year: Approximately 10000 kg fruit/ha/year in an established planting at 4 × 4 m (INPA).
Ideal Light Conditions: Full sun to light shade (inferred)
Ideal Soil Conditions: Naturally on seasonally flooded banks (várzea/igapó) but also grown on terra firme Latosol. Needs steady moisture; a mulch of dead vegetation cut water use by ~18% and helps in the dry season
Layout: 4 × 4 m on terra firme (Embrapa); 3 × 3 m used in Peruvian plantations, thinned to 6 × 3 m by year 10. Propagate from cuttings (with IBA) to keep selected traits
Intercrop: Not documented. (inferred) Short-cycle crops in early years
Companion Plants: Not documented. (inferred) Gliricidia or Ingá for mulch and nitrogen
Trees: Sparse legume shade trees (Ingá, Gliricidia); can be planted at the edge of ponds or flood-prone areas

Harvest Time: First cut ~1 year after planting (no use in year 1 so roots establish), then ~2–3 cuts/yr (every ~4–6 months) at ~50 cm height
Yield / Year: 5000–20000 kg dry matter/ha/year (team-cited Embrapa); approximately 4400 kg/ha/year in an Amazonian agroforestry system and 5800 kg/ha/year in alley cropping. EcoCrop separately reports 9000–16000 kg dry matter/ha or up to 43000 kg fresh material/ha, with no annual basis specified.
Ideal Light Conditions: Full sun; excess shade reduces growth
Ideal Soil Conditions: Drought-resistant and adaptable, tolerates low-fertility soils; avoid waterlogging (general knowledge). Fixes nitrogen; leaves ~3% N; use the numeric EcoCrop fields for environmental screening.
Layout: Hedgerows or alleys: 1 m between plants in the row, rows 3–6 m apart (3 × 1 m and 6 × 1 m used in trials); 0.5 m for dense fodder banks; 1–2 m for intercrops
Intercrop: Maize, beans, cassava (less competition than Leucaena), palma, sorghum, pasture in alleys
Companion Plants: Cubiu (its biomass suppresses Sclerotium), Banana, Cupuaçu, Crotalaria, pigeon pea
Trees: Itself a lopped nitrogen-fixing tree. Pairs with Ingá, banana, cupuaçu or coconut

Harvest Time: Fruits from year 3 (sometimes year 2). Fruit ripens ~6 months after flowering. Plant at the start of the rains
Yield / Year: ~5000–10000 kg/ha/yr in producing countries; ~6000 kg/ha in Cerrado; 23000 kg/ha at 4 years in an Embrapa Roraima trial. ~15 fruits/plant/yr is considered satisfactory
Ideal Light Conditions: (inferred) Full sun (young trees tolerate partial shade); warm, humid tropics
Ideal Soil Conditions: Deep, well-drained, fertile, sandy-clay soil, pH as specified in the numeric EcoCrop fields. Avoid waterlogging; use the numeric EcoCrop fields for environmental screening.
Layout: 5 × 5 to 6 × 6 m (up to 7 × 7 m). Pits 40–60 cm in each dimension with compost. Prune to a manageable height
Intercrop: (inferred) Banana, cassava or beans in the early years until the canopy closes
Companion Plants: Gliricidia, Ingá, pigeon pea, Crotalaria
Trees: Ingá and Gliricidia lopped for mulch; banana for early shade; cupuaçu in the lower layers

Harvest Time: Leaves from 2–3 months after planting cuttings, then continuous cutting of young shoots. Regular pruning stimulates new growth
Yield / Year: Documented edible shoot-tip production: 20,000 to 40,000 kg/ha/year with at least 4000 plants/ha and 5–8 cuts/year (Embrapa CT156); not equivalent to total leaves-plus-stems biomass.
Ideal Light Conditions: Best in full sun (heliophyte); tolerates half-shade. Seedlings did better under 30–50% shade
Ideal Soil Conditions: Rustic; grows in most soils without high fertility. Well-drained; use raised mounds in very wet soil. Optimum 25–30 °C, minimum ~10 °C. Drought-tolerant, tolerates light frost
Layout: Leaf production: 1–1.3 m between rows, 0.4–0.6 m between plants (UFRRJ). As a climber (Epagri): 1.5 m between rows, 2 m between plants, on a trellis. Thorny, so keep away from paths
Intercrop: Not documented. (inferred) Can be grown as a hedge or trellis along bed edges
Companion Plants: (inferred) Gliricidia or Crotalaria as nitrogen sources
Trees: (inferred) Climbs on a trellis, stakes or sparse trees such as Gliricidia . Prefers high light

Harvest Time: First harvest in year 1–2 after planting in a Manaus trial; capsules picked when dry. Long-lived (40–50 years)
Yield / Year: National average ~1,138 kg seed/ha; Amazônia in the range 300–1,200 kg/ha; ~580 kg seed/ha in year 2 in a Manaus agroforestry trial
Ideal Light Conditions: Full sun (needs high light); 20–26 °C optimum
Ideal Soil Conditions: Deep, well-drained, medium to clay soil without stones or laterite; low-fertility soils respond to fertilizer. Avoid waterlogging and cold nights; use the numeric EcoCrop fields for environmental screening.
Layout: 6 × 5 m traditional; 7 × 3, 6 × 3 or 5 × 2 m used for mechanization; 4 × 4 m in a cupuaçu–pupunha–Brazil nut system. Prune to keep a manageable height
Intercrop: Beans, maize, cassava in early years; cupuaçu, pupunha, Brazil nut (4 × 4 m system)
Companion Plants: Gliricidia, Crotalaria, pigeon pea
Trees: Plant at the sunny edge or between rows of cupuaçu, pupunha and Brazil nut in their early years; avoid shading by tall trees

Harvest Time: First harvest ~2 years after planting clones (small), average yields counted from year 3; several pickings per season, number depends on the clone
Yield / Year: ~1.5–3 kg dry seed/plant/yr (1.49–1.55 kg for BRS Amazonas/Maués; 1.9–3.1 kg for BRS Noçoquém) ≈ 600–1,250 kg/ha at 400 plants/ha. National average ~325 kg/ha
Ideal Light Conditions: Young plants are shaded; adult light needs not retrieved
Ideal Soil Conditions: Deep, well-drained, acidic terra firme soil (Latosol); prefers previously cultivated land or capoeira, not fresh forest clearing. Pits 40 × 40 × 40 cm, organic matter and phosphorus
Layout: 5 × 5 m (400 plants/ha); climbing shrub trained on stakes or supported by lopped trees. Clonal cuttings (7 months in the nursery) are preferred over seed
Intercrop: Not documented in sources retrieved. (inferred) Short-cycle crops between young plants
Companion Plants: Gliricidia, Ingá, Crotalaria for mulch and nitrogen (inferred)
Trees: Light shade from banana in early years and sparse legume trees (Ingá, Gliricidia)

Harvest Time: First crop ~2 years after planting (general knowledge); the second year starts the first fertilizer top-dressing in live-stake systems (Embrapa)
Yield / Year: Pará average ~2000–2300 kg/ha dry pepper (was 4000 kg/ha in the past); ~2 kg/plant for Cingapura-type cultivars in Rondônia
Ideal Light Conditions: Tolerates full sun with a live stake; best with partial shade from a pruned living support
Ideal Soil Conditions: Deep, well-drained, organic-rich soil, pH as specified in the numeric EcoCrop fields; avoid sandy or poorly drained soil (root rot). Needs warm, humid climate
Layout: 2.5 × 2.5 m (Embrapa), or 2 × 2 m in Tomé-Açu agroforestry; pits 40 cm in each direction. Train vines up a stake or live Gliricidia support kept pruned at ~2.2 m
Intercrop: Cupuaçu, cacao, açaí in agroforestry (Tomé-Açu), rice in the first year
Companion Plants: Gliricidia (live support; improves pepper quality), Crotalaria, pigeon pea
Trees: Gliricidia as live support (Embrapa Amazônia Oriental); avoid in monoculture with hardwood stakes, which require felling 25–30 trees/ha

Harvest Time: Leaves/tips: 60–90 days after planting, cutting branches 30–50 cm long, then continuous. Calyces: ~128–172 days after planting, picked in staggered harvests
Yield / Year: Approximately 1.5 kg fresh or 0.156 kg dry calyces/plant over five staggered harvests, versus approximately 0.6 kg fresh calyces/plant in a single harvest (UFLA trial).
Ideal Light Conditions: Full sun; short-day flowering plant. Needs high light for calyx production
Ideal Soil Conditions: Well-drained, fertile soil with organic matter; pH as specified in the numeric EcoCrop fields. Sensitive to salty irrigation water; use the numeric EcoCrop fields for environmental screening.
Layout: 1.0–1.5 m between plants (Embrapa). Cut branches at 30–50 cm for harvest. Plant on sunny edges of beds or tree rows. Embrapa alternatives: 1 × 0.5 m for leaves or 1 × 1 m for flowers.
Intercrop: Not documented. (inferred) Beans, maize or cassava while young
Companion Plants: Gliricidia, Crotalaria, pigeon pea (nitrogen fixers)
Trees: Gliricidia or Ingá, lopped heavily so enough light reaches it. Avoid dense shade

Harvest Time: Fruit from ~3–5 years after planting (general knowledge); fruiting is seasonal and varies by region. Thinning of extra stems yields palm heart
Yield / Year: ~8000 kg fruit/ha/yr in managed várzea stands (~2,700 bunches); also ~200 palm hearts/ha/yr from thinning. Terra firme yields depend on irrigation and spacing
Ideal Light Conditions: Full sun to light shade; growth rises with light up to an optimum below full irradiance; heavily shaded plants grow slowly
Ideal Soil Conditions: Naturally floodplain (várzea) and moist soils; also terra firme with irrigation and organic matter. Moist, fertile, well-drained to periodically flooded; use the numeric EcoCrop fields for environmental screening.
Intercrop: Cupuaçu, cacao, banana, papaya, passion fruit, Brazil nut, pigeon pea, cassava early on
Companion Plants: Banana, pigeon pea (temporary shade), Gliricidia, Ingá, Crotalaria
Trees: Itself the mid-to-upper palm layer; Brazil nut or Parica above, cupuaçu and cacao below. Increase spacing when interplanted

Harvest Time: First fruit approximately two years after planting (agroforestry guide); prune according to the intended shade or biomass system.
Yield / Year: 25000–30000 kg dry biomass/ha accumulated over 30 months at 2 × 2 m in an Embrapa improved-fallow system; not an annual yield and not applicable to the wider shade-tree layout.
Ideal Light Conditions: Full sun; fast-growing canopy shade tree
Ideal Soil Conditions: Adapts to poor, acidic, well-drained tropical soils; EcoCrop pH as specified in the numeric EcoCrop fields (tolerates 4.5–8.0). Fixes nitrogen; use the numeric EcoCrop fields for environmental screening.
Layout: Agroforestry guide: approximately 7 × 7 m for adult trees. Separate biomass/fallow system: 2 × 2 m; do not mix the associated yields.
Intercrop: Cupuaçu, cacao, coffee, banana, cariru, taioba
Companion Plants: Açaí, Gliricidia, Moringa
Trees: Paricá, Castanha-do-Pará, Açaí

Harvest Time: Grafted trees fruit from year 3–5 (seedlings 5–8). Fruit ripens 3–6 months after flowering, mainly summer to autumn
Yield / Year: ~100–250 fruits/tree/yr (5–30 kg each), roughly 10–25 t/ha at maturity
Ideal Light Conditions: Full sun when mature. Young trees tolerate partial shade
Ideal Soil Conditions: Deep, well-drained loam, pH as specified in the numeric EcoCrop fields, with 1,500+ mm rainfall. Moderately drought-tolerant once established; use the numeric EcoCrop fields for environmental screening.
Layout: 10 × 10 to 12 × 12 m. Restrain to ~6 m by pruning for easier harvest
Intercrop: Cacao, coffee, black pepper, pineapple, banana (early years), ginger, turmeric
Companion Plants: Inga, Gliricidia, pigeon pea, Canavalia, Crotalaria
Trees: Inga, açaí, cupuaçu in the lower layers. Avoid close planting with other large canopy trees

Harvest Time: First leaf cut 60–90 days after transplanting, then every 35–45 days. Pods from ~6–8 months
Yield / Year: ~10000–30000 kg/ha/yr fresh leaf in dense hedges. Pods ~3000–10000 kg/ha
Ideal Light Conditions: Full sun. Yield drops under heavy shade
Ideal Soil Conditions: Well-drained sandy loam, pH as specified in the numeric EcoCrop fields. Very drought-tolerant, highly intolerant of waterlogging; use the numeric EcoCrop fields for environmental screening.
Layout: Dense hedgerows at 1 × 0.5 m (leaf), or 3 × 3 m (pods). Also good as border or alley-crop rows
Intercrop: Cowpea, beans, sorghum, maize, cassava, okra, sweet potato
Companion Plants: Gliricidia, pigeon pea, Leucaena, Crotalaria
Trees: Sparse overstory only (Gliricidia, Inga lopped regularly). Suits the semi-arid Northeast and the Cerrado

Harvest Time: Palm heart first cut ~18–24 months after planting (up to 3 years), then annual cuts from new offshoots. Fruit from ~3–4 years (fruit varieties)
Yield / Year: Palm heart: 1000–1400 kg/ha at first cut; 1200–2000 kg/ha/year afterwards (Embrapa Acre/Rondônia); productive life approximately ten years.
Ideal Light Conditions: Full sun once established; young plants benefit from 30–50% shade in the first year
Ideal Soil Conditions: Rustic; tolerates acid, low-fertility soil but prefers fertile, medium-textured, well-drained soil; mean temperature ≥22 °C and 1,600–1,700 mm rain, well distributed; use the numeric EcoCrop fields for environmental screening.
Layout: n/a
Intercrop: Rice, maize, beans, cassava, pumpkin or pineapple in the first year; peanut (nitrogen-fixing) or sorghum (poor soil)
Companion Plants: Pueraria (green manure used with rubber–pupunha), peanut, Crotalaria, Gliricidia
Trees: Rubber (seringueira) in a rubber–pupunha system; cupuaçu, urucum and Brazil nut in multi-strata systems

Harvest Time: Timber ~8–15 years. Leaves and fruit as biopesticide material once mature
Yield / Year: ~15–25 m³/ha/yr (fast growth)
Ideal Light Conditions: Full sun
Ideal Soil Conditions: Tolerant of many soils, pH as specified in the numeric EcoCrop fields, prefers well-drained loam. Drought-tolerant; use the numeric EcoCrop fields for environmental screening.
Layout: 5 × 5 m, or lines at 8–10 m for windbreaks or alley systems
Intercrop: Beans, maize and cassava early on. Pasture (silvopasture), with livestock kept from fruit
Companion Plants: Inga, Gliricidia, pigeon pea, Crotalaria
Trees: Plant beside native trees such as ipê or Mimosa scabrella. Don't plant near forest edges (invasive risk)

Harvest Time: Native stands produce from year 12–14, planted trees from ~11 years. Timber possible from year 8 by thinning dense stands (4 × 4 m)
